| Role | Default agent | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Architect | Codex; scoped Claude exception for the v6.9 site mock-up work on `arch/canonical-v69-pivot` (2026-10-06; see below) | Creates feature maps, causal sequencing, protected seams, and feature-to-task guidance. |
| Planner | Codex (Claude exception ended at the 2026-10-03 21:23 reset; see below) | Converts reviewed feature guidance into small UI-verifiable task definitions. |
| Implementer | Claude | Builds the active task, runs checks, and prepares the review packet. |
| Reviewer | Configurable independent agent; Codex by default (see below) | Reviews work independently from the author. |

## Rules

- Keep role responsibilities stable even if the bound agent changes.
- Do not assume Planner, Architect, or Implementer means a specific vendor unless
  this file says so.
- Implementer may refine implementation steps, but should not redefine feature
  sequencing without Architect or user review.
- Reviewer must be independent from the agent that authored the implementation.
- Claude Code commands in `.claude/commands/` should read this file before
  acting so they can either run the role or prepare a handoff for the configured
  agent.

## Decision Requests Go To The Active Architect

Set by the owner on 2026-10-04 (verbatim in `.agent/owner-T028-closeout-2026-10-04.md`):
"for all decsion requests, let the active architect make them and inform me if
the architect wants me to weigh in as well with its justification and decision".

So the coordinator does not put decision requests to the owner. It sends them
to the Architect bound above, which decides, records the decision with its
justification, and informs the owner. Where the Architect wants the owner to
weigh in, it says so, giving its decision and justification, and the owner may
confirm or overrule. Owner acceptance of a slice (USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED) is not
a decision request and still goes to the owner.

## Invoking A Codex-Bound Role

A role bound to Codex is run by invoking Codex, not by dispatching the
same-named Claude subagent and merging what it returns. Codex is on PATH and
runs non-interactively:

```
codex exec "<the role brief>"
```

**The obligation is the coordinator's, not the subagent's.** On 2026-09-23 the
Architect correctly flagged three times that it was producing Architect output
while this file bound the role to Codex. Each time the coordinator relayed the
flag to the user as a question and merged the output anyway. A subagent noticing
a binding violation is not a control, because it has already done the work by
the time it can tell anyone. The control is that the coordinator invokes the
bound tool in the first place.

So: before dispatching `assetops-architect` or `assetops-planner`, check the
binding above. If it is Codex, run `codex exec`. The Claude subagents of those
names refuse Codex-bound work rather than producing it.

## The Reviewer Binding, And Its Backup

The Reviewer is **Codex by default**. When Codex is unavailable - usage limit,
outage, or a reset hours away - the backup is a **fresh Claude
`assetops-reviewer` subagent**, and the substitution needs no permission. A
slice waiting a day for quota is worse than a slice reviewed by the weaker of
two independent readers.

**Independence is the rule the backup must not break.** The backup is a NEW
agent instance. It is never the agent that implemented the slice, and never
that agent resumed with a different instruction. An implementer asked to
review its own work will confirm it, which is why the binding exists.

State in the report which reviewer produced it. A Claude review of Claude
implementation is genuinely weaker than a Codex one on the same slice, and a
later reader deciding how much weight to give a verdict needs to know which
they are reading. Where the substitution happened because of quota, say so and
say what was left unjudged, so the question can go back to Codex if it matters
enough to wait for.

## Which Reviewer For Which Round

Set by the user on 2026-09-26 to conserve Codex quota, which has been the
binding constraint on this milestone three times. This is not the same as the
backup rule above: it applies whether or not Codex is available.

**Codex reviews discovery.** The first review of any slice, a contract version
move, a new mechanism or a restructure, and any round where the Implementer had
to choose between legitimate treatments. T020B's R1 was that round - state a
rule for unaligned windows or refuse them at setup - and it needed the stronger
reader.

**A fresh Claude `assetops-reviewer` reviews verification.** A correction round
where an independent reviewer has already named the defects and the fix needs
no design choice: prose, docstrings, claim corrections, test assertions,
deletions. The job is confirming the named items closed and nothing else moved.
Fresh rather than resumed, because there is no context worth preserving for
checking named sentences and a clean reader is worth more.

The honest risk, recorded so it is not discovered later: this relies on the
previous review having found everything discoverable in that area. Four
consecutive rounds on T020B each found something the last missed, which is the
argument against cheap re-reviews. **So a Claude verification pass that finds
something unexpected is a signal to escalate that round back to Codex, not a
cheap verdict to accept.** Finding an unnamed defect means the round was
discovery after all and was misclassified.

Two classification traps worth naming, both seen on T020B:

- **A correction round can widen under the Implementer's hand.** The R1a/R1b
  round was three sentences and a deletion when dispatched; it came back having
  also corrected an unnamed fourth sentence and added a property-based guard
  over thirteen windows. Classify on what came back, not on what was sent.
- **"Small" will drift to "everything" if it is not tested against the two
  lists above.** The question is not how many lines changed. It is whether a
  reader had to decide anything.

## Do Not Write The Review In The Brief

Recorded on 2026-09-26 at the user's instruction, because this project had
been doing the opposite. Reviewer briefs had grown to eight numbered questions,
each naming the thing to judge and supplying the arguments on both sides. That
is not a brief; it is a draft verdict with blanks. A reviewer steered to eight
questions inspects eight things, and the ninth - the one nobody thought to ask
about - is the one that reaches production.

A brief gives the Reviewer:

- the target: branch, commit, spec, packet, and where prior reviews live;
- the standing criteria it is reviewing against, which live in the task file
  and this project's records, not in the brief;
- **what has already been run and verified**, with results, so quota is not
  spent re-running a green suite. This is factual and does not steer;
- the constraints: do not merge, do not fix, where to write, what not to touch.

A brief does **not** give the Reviewer:

- an enumerated list of what to judge;
- the arguments for or against a conclusion;
- which findings the coordinator considers important;
- a named preferred outcome, or a hint of one.

Pointing at an artifact is not steering; summarising what that artifact says is.
Where a genuine question must be asked - a decision only the user can take, a
constraint the Reviewer cannot infer - ask it plainly and separately, and do not
dress an opinion as a question.

The Implementer's packet already states its own uncertainties and residual
risks. That is the right channel for "look at this": the author declaring what
it is unsure of, in a document the Reviewer reads anyway.

## Sort Findings Before Forwarding Them

Recorded on 2026-09-26 after the user asked whether the Reviewer was applying
`D-2026-09-22-milestone-speed-over-purity`. It was; all three T020A1 reviews
cited it, and Codex used it to carry an HTTP-reachable 500, five overflow
sites and several residuals rather than block on them. **The coordinator was
the leak.**

That decision's stopping rule is narrow. Stop only for a defect expensive to
reverse, a claim that would mislead an Implementer, or a decision only the user
can take. **Everything else is recorded and carried.** A Reviewer that rates a
finding low and does not demand it has already applied the rule; forwarding it
as fix work overrides the Reviewer in the direction the decision forbids.

So when a review returns, the coordinator sorts every finding into block or
carry against those three conditions before putting any of it to the user, and
says which is which. A finding that is carried goes to
`.ai/MILESTONE_REVIEW_BACKLOG.md` with the reason, not into the next round.

T020A1 is the case to remember: five implementation rounds and three review
passes, of which two rounds closed comment counts, a docstring and a Draft
count that had drifted. Each was real. None was a reason to reopen a slice.

## Using Codex Efficiently

Codex quota is **account-level and shared across every model**. On 2026-09-24
it was exhausted twice in one day, the second time mid-review, and switching
to `gpt-6-sol`, `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-sol` and `gpt-5.5` all returned the
identical limit with the identical reset time. **You cannot route around an
exhausted limit by changing model.** The only lever is spending less per call,
before the limit is reached.

What it cost that day, measured from the run logs:

| Pass | Tokens | Shell calls | Started |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reviewer pass 1 | 145,247 | 31 | cold |
| Reviewer pass 2 | 145,568 | 38 | cold |
| Reviewer pass 3 | 25,259, then died | 5 | cold |

Pass 2 spent 145k tokens re-deriving what pass 1 had already established.

### Resume instead of restarting

`codex exec resume <session-id> "<follow-up prompt>"` continues an existing
session with its context intact. `--last` resumes the most recent. The session
id is printed in the header of every run, so **capture it whenever a Codex
role may be returned to** - which is every review, because a review that finds
defects is returned to by definition.

A second pass on the same slice is a follow-up, not a new engagement. Resume
it and say what changed. Start cold only when the subject is genuinely
different or the earlier session would mislead.

**`resume` does not take the same flags as `exec`, and this cost two failed
invocations on 2026-09-25 before it was pinned down.** Two rules:

- Options go **before** the session id: `codex exec resume [OPTIONS]
  <session-id> "<prompt>"`. After it they are parsed as the prompt.
- **`--sandbox` does not exist on `resume`.** Pass it as config instead:
  `-c sandbox_mode="workspace-write"`. `resume` accepts `-c`, `--last`,
  `--all`, `-m`, `--skip-git-repo-check`, `--json`, `-o` and a few others;
  run `codex exec resume --help` rather than assuming a flag carries over.

The working form, verified:

```
codex exec resume -c sandbox_mode="workspace-write" --skip-git-repo-check   <session-id> "<follow-up prompt>" < /dev/null
```

Both failures were argument parsing, rejected before any model call, so they
cost seconds and no quota. The point of recording them is that guidance which
fails on first use is worse than none.

A session resumes across a quota interruption: the third-pass review that died
mid-run at its usage limit was resumed the next day into the same session id
with its context intact.

### Match the model to the work

`-m <model>` selects one. `gpt-6-astra` is the default and the most expensive;
`gpt-6-sol` is the workhorse coding model; `gpt-6-luna` is the cheap one. Full
list: `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6-sol`, `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.6-terra`,
`gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.5`.

Reserve Astra for genuine architecture and review judgement. Mechanical passes
- a fix round against a written list, a routine Planner expansion, a
consistency sweep - do not need it.

### Never spend a full session on a probe

`~/.codex/config.toml` sets `model_reasoning_effort = "high"` globally, while
the models' own default is `low`. A one-line availability probe therefore runs
at high reasoning. If you must probe, use
`-m gpt-6-luna -c model_reasoning_effort=low`. Better: attempt the real work
and detect the limit from the error, which costs nothing when the limit is
already hit.

### Put verification in the brief, not in the session

Every fact the brief states is work the session does not repeat. Say what you
already ran and what you already verified - test counts, check results,
confirmed line numbers - and say plainly that repeating it is not wanted.
Ask Codex for judgement, not for re-running a green suite.

### Invocation mechanics that have already gone wrong

- **Pass the prompt as an argument, never on stdin.** `codex exec ... - < file`
  blocked for three hours with no output on 2026-09-23. Always redirect
  `< /dev/null`.
- **Do not double-background.** `nohup codex ... &` inside an already
  backgrounded call returns instantly, and the harness reports a completion
  that has not happened. Background the call once.
- **A branch carries a snapshot of these rules.** A session started on a task
  branch reads that branch's `.ai/`, not main's. Merge main into the branch
  before a review if a rule has changed.

## Using The Claude Implementer Efficiently

Set by the owner on 2026-09-29 after T023, T022B and T024 each cost 80-200M
re-read tokens and one to three hours. Measured from the transcripts: cost is
context size times turns, and context grew from resumed agents and from source
code read whole into context. The agent's own rules are in
`.claude/agents/assetops-implementer.md` "Context budget"; these are the
coordinator's:

- **A fresh implementer per build and per fix round. Never resume one.**
  T024's build started at 209k tokens because the read-only planning agent was
  resumed; T023's fix rounds started at 458k. If a slice needs a planning pass,
  the planner writes its plan to `.agent/T0NN-implementer-plan.md` and a fresh
  agent builds from that file.
- **Fix rounds run on Sonnet** (`model: sonnet` on dispatch), briefed with the
  review file and the findings to fix. New slices stay on the session model,
  where design judgement matters.
- **Keep slices small.** A task the implementer sizes at several times a
  previous slice is a split candidate before it is built, not after.
- **Build large slices in phases, a fresh agent per phase.** Set by the owner
  on 2026-09-29 after T025a: bounded reads cut read volume by about two thirds,
  but 508 turns still took context to 467k and cost 142M re-read tokens,
  because cost grows with the square of the turn count. A slice beyond one
  focused change is dispatched as phases (for example contracts and core, then
  model and setup, then Lab and frontend). Each phase ends with committed work
  and a short handoff at `.agent/T0NN-phase-N-handoff.md` (what landed, file
  anchors, what is next, open risks); the coordinator dispatches a fresh agent
  for the next phase from that file. Full suites and the packet belong to the
  last phase.
- **Hand off at about 120k context.** Set by the owner on 2026-10-02 after
  usage showed 66% of tokens spent above 150k context and 67% in implementer
  subagents. An implementer that nears 120k commits what is safe, writes its
  handoff and stops, even mid-phase; a fresh agent continues from the handoff.
  The coordinator plans phases so that none is expected to reach that size,
  splitting a phase into sub-phases (2a, 2b) rather than letting one run long.
- **Backend tests: focused per phase, full once per slice** (OPS-01,
  `backend/TESTING.md`). Each phase runs the focused and adjacent backend files
  it touched; the real-Postgres full suite runs once per slice, on the final
  revision, with the guide's normal command and JUnit zero-skip check.
  Reviewers (Claude or Codex) cite that same-revision full evidence and run
  focused files; they rerun the full suite only for a finding that needs it.
  Before any full run start `tools/keep-awake-during-tests.ps1` and cap the run
  at twice its expected wall time; a run past the cap is stopped and reported,
  never waited on. One full suite on this machine at a time.
- **Mechanical sub-steps run on Sonnet.** Work fixed by an agreed contract or
  handoff - tests written against a settled interface, an AC-by-AC evidence
  pass, closeout records - is dispatched with `model: sonnet`, like fix rounds.
  Steps that decide a design stay on the session model.

## Token Efficiency Without Lowering Quality (owner, 2026-10-18)

Owner: be very efficient without compromising quality, in every session. Lessons
from W1 rework and W2-00..W2-03 (about 30-40% avoidable rework, then 15-20%):

- **All acceptance rules in the brief from the start.** Layout contract,
  recurring-defect checklist, height rule, plain-language rules, proof list.
  Never introduce a rule mid-build; it forces trimming passes on every slice.
- **Build specs answer the known question classes before coding.** A W2+ build
  spec is ready only when it fixes, against the actual code: identifier
  grammars and formats; exact fixture Site/Foundation values and how bindings
  are published; every seam with path:symbol; guard allowlists the new code
  must satisfy (rule 8 writers, sqlalchemy import allowlist, dependency
  direction); refusal codes; freshness/time references; UI empty/unavailable
  copy and the panel map; how Lab/run projections and stored artifacts look.
  W2-02 needed six question rounds because its first spec skipped these.
  Then the Architect does an **implementer dry-read**: walk the spec commit by
  commit against the real code, write down every question a mid-level
  implementer would have to ask (multiplicity such as per-connector channels,
  which component owns each device, new Foundation keys, readiness codes for
  each missing input, cadence sources, fixture Sites vs revisions, migration
  numbering against in-flight slices), and answer each in the spec. W2-05a
  stopped with eight such questions after the gate alone.
- **Size builder runs to one spec commit each**, with a handoff after each, so
  no run dies mid-commit and the next run reads only the handoff.
- **Model by risk.** First review of a new build and design-deciding work on
  the session model; fix rounds, re-reviews (scoped to prior findings) and
  mechanical steps on Sonnet. A capture- or copy-only fix may be verified by
  the coordinator directly (view the evidence, record a short verify note).
- **Serialize slices that edit the same shared UI files**; parallelize only
  disjoint work (backend vs frontend, different domains).
- **One full suite per round, only when no builder is running.** Do not rerun
  full suites after doc-, test- or CSS-only changes; rerun the touched files.
- **Batch Architect/Planner questions into one Codex call**, and fold a
  preemptive sweep of the slice's remaining commits into that same call.
- **No duplicate agents.** Check for a live agent on a worktree before
  dispatching; never reuse a worktree a reviewer is still using.
- **Mockup drives the design; implementers never decide (owner, 2026-10-18).**
  Every spec maps each mock panel, row, column and chip of each owned screen to
  its data source or an honest gap; no mock element is trimmed or redesigned to
  fit the backend. Any implementer choice the spec did not fix is a defect:
  reviewers flag it Medium (High if user-visible vs the mock), and the Architect
  rules it and amends the spec before merge
  (`.agent/owner-fidelity-and-design-ownership-2026-10-18.md`).
- **Briefs point to files; they do not restate them.** Coordinator replies to
  interim agent notifications stay to one line.

## Updating Bindings

Change bindings here when the team wants a different tool to own a role. Record
material changes in `.ai/DECISIONS.md` if they affect workflow, review
independence, or task ownership.

## Selection, projection and capability

One `ColdSelection` has `tenant_id,site_id,code,from_at,to_at,known_at,watermark,foundation_revision_ids,binding_revision_ids,assessment_revision_id,finding_revision_ids,source_gate`. `from_at` and `to_at` are UTC and half-open; `known_at` defaults to latest committed disposition watermark captured once at request start. Omitted `from,to` selects W2-03's latest settled cold window; exactly one omitted is 422. The effective Foundation/binding is selected at each evidence source time (W2-03), with the selected policy at the requested window; conflicting/absent effective revision is an explicit limitation. 31 days maximum. No newer assessment, Finding or consequence may be silently mixed with an older `known_at`. A late accepted report makes the current projection `PENDING_RECOMPUTE` until a new exact assessment and cold consequence both settle. A selected old cutoff is `HISTORICAL`, even when there is no pending work. Determine probe freshness from the latest qualifying accepted probe `source_time` within `[from,to)` compared with `to`: over 10 minutes is `STALE_SOURCE`. Later wall-clock viewing of the 2026-10-06 replay never alone makes it stale or live. Precedence: overlapping queued/failed newer work -> `PENDING_RECOMPUTE`; explicit cutoff older than latest relevant committed disposition -> `HISTORICAL`; no settled selection/probe or future `to` -> `UNKNOWN`; old last probe -> `STALE_SOURCE`; otherwise `CURRENT`. Money can remain `UNPRICED` within a current technical read; pending/old/unresolved money has its own withholding limit.

`ColdSiteReadService` joins, by exact UUIDs, W2-03 `ColdReadService` output, W2-01 Foundation, S4-05 source/publication links and the cold consequence head. It does not use a display-name join or the latest Finding irrespective of window. Capability claims are exactly `TEMPERATURE_POINT,EXCURSION_BOUNDS,BACKUP_START_RESULT,TRANSFER_POSITION,COOLING_RESPONSE,PRODUCT_EXPOSURE`. Each has `state:SUPPORTED|LIMITED|UNAVAILABLE|CONTRADICTORY`, `required_roles:string[]`, `missing_roles:string[]`, `coverage:{known_points:int,expected_points:int,ratio:decimal string}` and `as_of,limitation`. `TEMPERATURE_POINT` requires GOOD calibrated room probe and attested clock; `EXCURSION_BOUNDS` adds policy, two qualifying samples and >=0.8 coverage with no >10-minute bridge; `BACKUP_START_RESULT` requires correlated accepted request/result and the W2-03 causal rules; `TRANSFER_POSITION` needs its own bound transfer report; `COOLING_RESPONSE` needs an accepted compressor state and probe series; `PRODUCT_EXPOSURE` means bounded thermal exposure only and requires an eligible excursion. Contradictory accepted facts give `CONTRADICTORY`, not healthy/failure. Source `contact` derives from a diagnostic received no later than selected `known_at` only when that diagnostic actually identifies the source; if only gateway-level contact exists, source contact is `UNKNOWN` with a limitation. `fact_age` is a nonnegative integer number of seconds/null between selected `to` and the last accepted source fact in `[from,to)` at the cutoff; it is distinct from contact. No source contact becomes equipment condition. Panel 3's â€œnext evidenceâ€ is simply a named missing role/link, never a scored recommendation.

Analysis rows are selected accepted public records from the pinned assessment basis and exact links, ordered `(source_time,evidence_id)`, with `evidence_id,kind,source_time,received_at,quality,role,exclusion,source_id,envelope_sha256,assessment_revision_id`; `exclusion` is W2-03's SUPPORT/CONTEXT/EXCLUDED reason or null. Keep a record in the list when excluded, label why, and link to the existing Site Evidence exact record when source gate permits. `claim_rules` lists rule ID `cold-excursion/1` or `cold-start-response/1`, requirement, observed/missing role, coverage and resulting limit, all derived from the selected assessment; no speculative prose rule. Opaque cursor encodes `(source_time,evidence_id)` and selected basis SHA; mismatch returns 409 rather than changing pages.

## Money schema `0023` and rules

Create four new tables (do not widen the mini-grid `financial_consequence_revision`, whose CHECK constrains `POTENTIAL_FUEL_COST`, `fuel-cost-1`, L and priced amount). The Site FK uses `(tenant_id,site_id)` -> `site(tenant_id,id)`; references to FindingRevision, cold episode revision, assessment revision and accepted evidence use composite `(tenant_id,site_id,id)` keys; the source link uses `(tenant_id,site_id,batch_id)`. Add scoped unique targets to referenced tables only where `0022` has not already supplied them. All tables have `tenant_id,site_id`; every immutable row has server `created_at`/`finished_at`, with UPDATE/DELETE refusal triggers. Downgrade refuses while any of these rows exist; otherwise drops only W2-04 triggers/tables/indexes, including its added scoped unique target on the older link table.

* `cold_consequence_revision`: `id uuid PK`, `finding_revision_id`, `episode_revision_id`, `assessment_revision_id` UUID NOT NULL; `revision_no int >0`, `prior_revision_id uuid NULL`; `kind` CHECK `PRODUCT_EXPOSURE|RECORDED_REPAIR`; `state` CHECK `UNPRICED|WITHHELD`; `reason` nonempty; `window_start,window_end timestamptz` with start<end; `room_asset_id uuid`; `overlap_group text`; `quantity_unit` CHECK `degC_min|none`; `quantity_low,quantity_high numeric NULL` nonnegative/ordered; `amount_low,amount_high numeric NULL`, `currency char(3) NULL`; `finding_basis_sha256,consequence_basis_sha256 char(64)`, `model_id` CHECK `cold-exposure/1|cold-repair/1`; `source_classification`, `source_gate_sha256 char(64)`, `assumption_revision_ids jsonb` array, `limitation text NULL`. Unique `(finding_revision_id,kind,revision_no)`, `(finding_revision_id,kind,consequence_basis_sha256)` and scoped `(tenant_id,site_id,id)` for evidence links. DB CHECK requires `amount_low IS NULL AND amount_high IS NULL AND currency IS NULL` for every row; a later approved migration must widen this. `quantity_unit='none'` requires both quantity bounds null; `degC_min` allows null bounds only when the technical claim is limited/withheld. No `RECORDED_REPAIR` row is created for the six replays because no exact accepted cost/work feed exists. `PRODUCT_EXPOSURE` may carry nonnegative bounded `degC_min`; if insufficient evidence both bounds null. No zero amount or stock count stands for unknown.
* `cold_consequence_evidence`: `consequence_revision_id,evidence_id,use,reason` with PK `(consequence_revision_id,evidence_id,use)`, `use=SUPPORT|CONTEXT|EXCLUDED` and scoped FKs. Include all exact evidence cited by the pinned Finding/episode basis, no private world keys.
* `cold_consequence_work`: `id uuid PK`, `cause` CHECK `FINDING_REVISION_APPENDED|EPISODE_REVISION_APPENDED|SOURCE_GATE_CHANGED`; nullable `finding_revision_id`, `episode_revision_id`, `publication_batch_id`, with a CHECK requiring exactly the locator for its cause, and scoped FKs; `window_start,window_end` (nonempty, half-open), `room_asset_id`, `dirty_key_sha256 char(64)`, `enqueued_at`; unique `(tenant_id,site_id,dirty_key_sha256)` and `(tenant_id,site_id,id)` for attempts. Add `(tenant_id,site_id,batch_id)` uniqueness to `batch_publication_link` in 0023 for the scoped `publication_batch_id` FK; `batch_id` is that table's actual PK, there is no link `id`. Trigger-only INSERT with `ON CONFLICT (tenant_id,site_id,dirty_key_sha256) DO NOTHING`. A cold FindingRevision or episode revision enqueues its selected Site/window/room; the source-gate trigger enqueues only overlapping heads. No runtime work insert/status update. Backfill existing W2-03 cold heads once during upgrade, idempotently. `0010_financial_assumptions` has a diesel-only DB CHECK as well as a diesel-only publisher: **no `ASSUMPTION_PUBLISHED` cause or trigger in 0023**. A future cold assumption contract must migrate the DB, publisher and dirty-work cause together.
* `cold_consequence_work_attempt`: `id uuid PK`, `work_id` scoped FK, `attempt_no int >0`, `outcome` CHECK `SUCCEEDED|FAILED`, `error_code text NULL`, `consequence_revision_ids jsonb` array, `finished_at`; unique `(work_id,attempt_no)`. Success has no error and exact returned IDs; failure has error and empty IDs. A failed attempt leaves work pending; pending means no successful attempt. Index `(site_id,enqueued_at)` and `(work_id,attempt_no DESC)`.

`overlap_group = 'cold:' + sha256(canonical JSON array [tenant_id,site_id,window_start,window_end,room_asset_id])`: literal lowercase `cold:` prefix, then 64 lowercase hex characters; it is a grouping label, not a V4 event/correlation ID (whose grammar excludes `:`). An excursion and backup Finding of the same selected room/window share it; the financial read groups `PRODUCT_EXPOSURE` by this key and takes the single selected excursion exposure basis, never sums both. The start-response Finding may carry a `WITHHELD` context consequence with the same key but zero *counted* exposure entries, not a numeric zero. No cross-window summing without an explicit disjoint-window contract.

The source-gate event is an appended `batch_publication_link` to a previously accepted cold batch, if one exists; its trigger selects only cold heads whose linked accepted IDs use that batch and enqueues `SOURCE_GATE_CHANGED` inside the link transaction. An initial link before acceptance has no heads and creates no money work; later W2-03 Finding/episode append enqueues it. `evidence_publication` is immutable and a new unrelated publication never dirties an existing cold basis. Each trigger derives the same canonical dirty key from `(cause,locator,tenant_id,site_id,window_start,window_end,room_asset_id)` and takes a Site advisory transaction lock before selecting heads, following `0012_evidence_consequence_work.py`'s enqueue lock pattern. The FindingRevision trigger is restricted to `NEW.domain='cold_chain'`. An episode with no warranted Finding still enqueues; the worker records a successful no-op attempt with an empty consequence ID array. No trigger on an accepted disposition bypasses W2-03 assessment: it waits for the new exact cold Finding/episode revision.

`cold-exposure/1` derives observed rectangle degree-minute bounds only from W2-03's persisted episode bounds/accepted evidence, not a continuous curve. A bounded positive or zero technical quantity is allowed only when W2-03 actually proved it; missing-probe/contradictory has null quantity. `PRODUCT_EXPOSURE` is unpriced for sound technical bounds because no `cold_stock_quantity`, `cold_stock_unit_value`, reviewed `cold_exposure_rule`, product/currency binding or source-gated valuation exists. These are **reserved future scenario keys**, displayed as missing, not publishable via the diesel-price publisher. Product value/currency and EV tariff would be explicitly authored scenario assumptions and still would not prove sales, collections, spoilage or lost revenue. Recorded repair needs an accepted exact cost/currency/work record; none of the six replay cases has one. Mixed/unknown source, closed S4-05 gate, stale/pending assessment, incomplete period or contradictory evidence yields `WITHHELD` and null amount. LR current-money gate also refuses a current money claim from historical/pending basis. `exact_basis` returns selected Finding/episode/assessment UUIDs, accepted evidence UUIDs, source gate digest, assumption revision UUIDs (empty in W2) and consequence basis SHA. Basis SHA hashes canonical sorted IDs, window/cutoff, model/formula version, quantity bounds, source gate and missing assumption markers; an identical basis returns the existing ID and a changed basis appends a new revision.

`PostgresConsequenceStore` alone inserts `cold_consequence_revision`, `cold_consequence_evidence` and `cold_consequence_work_attempt`; add separate cold methods without changing the existing mini-grid methods. `cold_recompute.process_one` selects unfinished work under `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('cold_consequence:' || work_id,0))`, takes one repeatable-read snapshot, refuses a foreign/missing exact basis, writes consequence/links and `SUCCEEDED` attempt in one transaction. On derivation failure it rolls back that transaction and appends a typed `FAILED` attempt in a fresh transaction. A crash before success commits leaves no partial revision; retries are idempotent. `run` uses the existing `financials/recompute.py:retry_due_at` 1,2,4,8,16-minute schedule and bounded batch; one bad work item cannot starve others. Trigger-created work does not depend on a successful worker.

## Five API reads

`cold_site_api.py:build_cold_site_router` mounts five GET paths below `/api/sites/{site_code}/cold`. Request query for all is optional paired `from,to`, optional `known_at` (strict UTC); Analysis additionally `cursor,limit` (default 50, max 200), matching W2-03's paging spelling. Use W2-03 shared common envelope exactly: `site_id,window:{from,to,known_at},currentness:{state,watermark,latest_relevant_evidence_at,pending_since},source_provenance:{classification,source_ids,evidence_ids,basis_sha256},limitations`. Every card/object includes `as_of` and `limitation`; scalar decimals serialize as decimal strings and absent values as JSON null. `currentness.state` is `CURRENT|PENDING_RECOMPUTE|STALE_SOURCE|HISTORICAL|UNKNOWN`. Valid empty selection is 200 with `UNKNOWN` and empty arrays. Use one selected repeatable-read snapshot for W2-03, source disclosure and consequence heads. No previous consequence becomes a current money claim while a relevant cold work item is queued or failed. Errors use `{error:{code,message}}`; never downgrade 503 into a blank page.

Refusal code contract (same scope and parse semantics as `cold_assessment_api.py:build_cold_assessment_router`): 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`; 403 `SITE_SCOPE_FORBIDDEN` or `COLD_SOURCE_DISCLOSURE_FORBIDDEN`; 404 `SITE_NOT_FOUND`; 409 `COLD_SELECTION_UNSETTLED` for an explicitly requested revision that has no settled exact basis or `COLD_CURSOR_BASIS_CHANGED` for a changed Analysis basis; 422 `COLD_TIME_INVALID`, `COLD_WINDOW_INVALID`, `COLD_WINDOW_TOO_LONG`, `COLD_PARAMETER_UNKNOWN`, `COLD_LIMIT_INVALID`, or `COLD_CURSOR_INVALID`; 503 `COLD_READ_UNAVAILABLE`. A wrong-type/foreign Site is 404 after access is checked. An absent optional current basis is 200 `UNKNOWN`, not a 409. Analysis cursor is unpadded base64url of sorted, compact UTF-8 JSON `{basis:<64 lowercase hex>,id:<UUID string>,t:<UTC instant>}`; malformed is 422 and an exact basis mismatch is 409. No arbitrary `after` offset or page across a changed basis.

| GET suffix | Exact additional response |
| --- | --- |
| `/overview` | `status:{state:OBSERVED_EXCURSION|NO_EXCURSION_OBSERVED|UNKNOWN|CONTRADICTORY,claim_level,as_of,limitation}`, `objective:{text,policy_low_deg_c,policy_high_deg_c,room_asset_id,as_of,limitation}`, `temperature_summary:{latest_deg_c,latest_at,coverage:{known_points,expected_points,ratio},episode_count,claim_level,as_of,limitation}`, `backup_summary:{attempts,observed_success,observed_failure,unknown,latest_chain_id,as_of,limitation}`, `causal_strip:[{step:GRID|START_REQUEST|START_RESULT|GENERATOR|TRANSFER|BUS|COMPRESSOR|PROBE,state:OBSERVED|MISSING|CONTRADICTORY,at,evidence_id,as_of,limitation}]`, `findings:{count,items:[{finding_id,revision_id,title,claim_level,link}],as_of,limitation}`, `needs_attention:[{code,text,link,as_of,limitation}]`, `consequence_summary:{state:UNPRICED|WITHHELD|UNKNOWN,quantity:{low,high,unit:'degC_min'|null},amount:{low:null,high:null,currency:null},overlap_group,as_of,limitation}`, `links:{temperature,backup,findings,evidence,analysis,financials}`. The response includes W2-03 selected temperature points only through its linked read, never repackages model truth. |
| `/evidence` | `capabilities:[{claim,state,required_roles,missing_roles,coverage,as_of,limitation}]`, `sources:[{id,role,contact,fact_age,accepted_count,last_accepted_at,as_of,limitation}]`, `links:{analysis,foundation,temperature,backup}`. `contact` is `RECENT|STALE|NEVER|UNKNOWN`; `fact_age` is duration/null, never equipment condition. |
| `/evidence/analysis` | `accepted_records:{items:[{evidence_id,kind,source_time,received_at,quality,role,exclusion,source_id,envelope_sha256,assessment_revision_id,link,as_of,limitation}],next_cursor}`, `claim_rules:[{rule_id,requirement,observed_roles,missing_roles,coverage,result,as_of,limitation}]`, `links:{evidence,findings}`. No private oracle or rejected ordinal masquerades as accepted. |
| `/financials` | `consequences:[{id,kind,state,quantity_bounds:{low,high},quantity_unit,amount_bounds:{low:null,high:null},currency:null,reason,overlap_group,exact_basis,as_of,limitation}]`, `not_included:[{code:STOCK_VALUE_UNDECLARED|EXPOSURE_RULE_UNAPPROVED|SPOILAGE_UNPROVED|REPAIR_COST_ABSENT|SOURCE_GATE_WITHHELD,text,as_of,limitation}]`, `links:{assumptions,findings,evidence}`. Return one counted exposure per overlap group; the optional backup context row is marked nonadditive. |
| `/financial-assumptions` | `items:[{key,revision_id,value,unit,currency,valid_from,valid_to,recorded_at,source,as_of,limitation}]`, `missing_keys:['cold_stock_quantity','cold_stock_unit_value','cold_exposure_rule']` in this slice, `publication_state:'NOT_SUPPORTED_IN_W2'`, `links:{financials}`. `items=[]` for six canonical replays. This is a read-only explicit absence statement, not a publication form. |

Links carry the exact selected `from,to,known_at` and record/revision ID through route builders, URL encoded. The Site overview's Finding count counts distinct current Finding IDs, not episode revisions. `needs_attention` is ordered: pending recompute, probe gap, observed start failure, unknown transfer, missing policy; omit a code only when its predicate is false. No â€œnext actionâ€ link unless an actual W2-03 Finding or Evidence destination exists.

## Fixtures, named tests and guards

Use `contract-fixtures/w2/cold/{normal,excursion,backup-failed,missing-probe,late-reading,contradictory}.json` (`cold-replay-manifest/1`) through registered Lab, Stage, gateway Batch V2 and ordinary S2 acceptance; never seed accepted rows. The fixture Site is `COLD-LAB-001` (`COLDCHAIN`, simulated source), imported from `backend/tests/fixtures/w2/cold-lab-001.yaml`: `room-1`, `probe-1`, `ambient-1`, `compressor-1`, `transfer-1`, `generator-1`, `bus-1`, `grid-1`; door forcing `door-1` resolves to the room sensor. The thirteen required frozen values are room capacity `1.2 kWh/degC`, leak `0.08 kW/degC`, door heat `0.02 kWh/min`, control low/high `2/4 degC`, policy low/high `2/4 degC`, minimum excursion `15 min`, return hysteresis `0.2 degC`; probe error `0.1 degC`; compressor cooling `3 kW`, start delay `1 min`; generator start timeout `5 min`. Import/conversion at `2026-10-01T00:00:00Z` is historical v3 compatible; `sites/binding_service.py:BindingService.publish` publishes eleven live v4-mapped channels at `2026-10-01T00:01:00Z` before the run. The six strict `cold-scenario/1` documents start `2026-10-06T19:00:00Z`, end `20:00:00Z`, seed `20417`, model `cold-thermal/1`, publication `cold-publication/1`, observation `cold-observation/1`; the immutable run identity pins Foundation, binding, scenario and observation digests. W2-04 consumes its public accepted IDs and W2-03 exact revision IDs, not the frozen private forcing or run trajectory.

Fixed selected window `[2026-10-06T19:00:00Z,2026-10-06T20:05:00Z)`, 13 five-minute points. Normal: 13/13, `NO_EXCURSION_OBSERVED`, observed start/transfer, no exposure Finding, no amount. Excursion: first high 19:15, open episode, lower duration 45 min, upper null, one unpriced `PRODUCT_EXPOSURE` group. Backup-failed: `OBSERVED_FAILURE`, door CONTEXT, same exposure group counted once. Missing-probe: 7/13, temperature `UNKNOWN`, quantity/amount null, start failure still observed. Late-reading: 20:05 cutoff 12/13 (19:20 held), 20:10 13/13 and new immutable assessment/consequence basis, old cutoff historical. Contradictory: `CONTRADICTORY`, no observed failure or priced amount. W2-02 manifests pin canonical envelope/batch hashes, dispositions, accepted IDs and public digest; W2-03 pins assessment/episode/Finding revisions. W2-04 stores only its own consequence revisions, evidence links, trigger work and attempts. Values and IDs come from accepted replay, not mock illustrations.

## Final Architect rulings on commit 1 (Q1-Q10)

This section overrides shorthand above where the two differ. Migration `0023` on `task/W2-04-cold-site-evidence-money` is provisional until its listed corrections are made; passing migration tests do not waive them.

1. **Q1 CHANGE â€” selected window and room.** Keep `assessment_revision.window_start/window_end` for each trigger; neither episode bounds nor `window_assessment_revision_id` is a money window. For an `EXCURSION`, `cold_episode.asset_id` is the room. For a `START_RESPONSE`, that asset and the start Finding's `subject_asset_id` are the **generator**, so they must never fill `room_asset_id` or the overlap key. Resolve the effective chamber room from the exact assessment's selected `cold-roles-1` Foundation/binding basis (the same room that its temperature policy names); require one scoped room, or raise and roll back. Apply this to the Finding trigger, episode trigger, source-gate trigger and backfill. Prove that excursion and start Finding for one assessment produce the same room/window/group and that no generator ID is stored as a room.
2. **Q2 ACCEPT.** Source-gate link dirties latest cold episode heads citing the batch through `cold_episode_evidence` and latest cold Finding heads citing it through `finding_revision_evidence`. Scope every subquery by tenant and Site as well as parent ID; distinct heads may produce distinct work rows but identical selected consequence basis returns the same revision.
3. **Q3 CHANGE â€” preserve instant precision.** Canonical JSON array of strings and lowercase hyphenated UUIDs stand. Use UTC `Z` timestamps with six fractional digits **when microseconds are nonzero**, and whole seconds otherwise. This selected-window key is distinct from `source_envelope.instant_text`, which emits whole seconds for envelope publication; W2-03's `_instant` accepts fractional selected bounds. Reject precision beyond microseconds at the API boundary; never truncate a selected window to seconds when hashing. The six replay windows happen to have whole seconds. SQL and Python golden vectors must match for whole-second and fractional inputs.
4. **Q4 ACCEPT with meaning.** `limitation IS NOT NULL` means a named technical limit, not an arbitrary note. For an open W2-03 excursion with lower `degC_min` and null upper, keep `UNPRICED`, store that partial bound and a nonempty `OPEN_EPISODE_UPPER_UNKNOWN` limitation. `WITHHELD` may have either/both null bounds. A sound closed exposure has both. Null amount/currency remains mandatory in every case.
5. **Q5 ACCEPT each extra.** Keep scoped self-FK, first-revision/prior-link CHECK, kind/model pairing, nonnull scoped room FK on revision and work, and nullable evidence-link reason. Add a same-Finding/kind predecessor check in store logic; FK alone does not prove chain membership. A successful no-Finding episode gets a no-op attempt, not a fabricated Finding or consequence.
6. **Q6 ACCEPT.** The listed `DEFAULT clock_timestamp()` columns, including evidence-link `created_at`, are server times. The sole store writer must omit them, and tests must assert they lie in the DB transaction's observed interval. Do not accept client timestamps in store methods. A forcing trigger is unnecessary for this owner-restricted append-only table.
7. **Q7 CHANGE â€” constrain the aggregate.** `source_classification` is exactly `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION|REGISTERED_SIMULATION|MIXED|UNKNOWN`, the values returned by `evidence/source_provenance.py`; add a SQL CHECK. `ATTESTED_REAL_SOURCE` is not a current class. Preserve reason/detail and exact IDs separately; `UNKNOWN` and `MIXED` withhold money.
8. **Q8 ACCEPT.** Missing room or invalid assessment window is an invariant violation: raise and roll back the W2-03 assessment/Finding transaction, following `0012` rather than silently dropping dirty work. The worker reports `FAILED` for later derivation faults; it cannot repair a missing enqueue.
9. **Q9 ACCEPT with a nonvacuous guard.** Rule 8 scans runtime modules, so inspect the exact `0023` migration separately. Require at least one `INSERT INTO cold_consequence_work`, and require every such INSERT to use `ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, site_id, dirty_key_sha256) DO NOTHING`; reject `DO UPDATE`, another arbiter or a missing INSERT. Probe by mutating a temporary copy of the migration and restoring it, with pass and fail cases; no probe may pass solely because migrations are skipped by the runtime scan.
10. **Q10 ACCEPT staged enforcement.** Commit 1 installs table/owner/probe-name registration and refuses foreign and mutating writes. Commit 2 adds real store INSERTs and enables per-table `inserts seen` assertions for revision, evidence and attempt. Before commit 2 is declared done, all three must be nonvacuously seen; no empty/fake SQL is allowed to satisfy the guard. The trigger-only work check is active in commit 1.

## Implementer dry-read: exact backend behavior

| Question a builder would otherwise decide | Binding answer and proof |
| --- | --- |
| Which Finding gets an exposure revision? | Only a selected, warranted `EXCURSION` FindingRevision with an exact `claim.episode_revision_id` and eligible episode. `START_RESPONSE` is chronology/context; do not emit the optional context consequence in W2-04. A successful start, unsupported excursion, or missing-probe episode without a Finding produces no consequence and may close its trigger work with an empty-ID success attempt. This avoids a second counted exposure and an invented zero row. |
| Which assessment is exact? | Join FindingRevision `assessment_revision_id`, `claim.episode_revision_id`, episode revision `assessment_revision_id`, and the selected W2-03 assessment pair by scoped IDs. A mismatch is a typed worker failure `COLD_BASIS_MISMATCH`, never a latest-row fallback. For a source-gate event, re-read the latest settled heads at its transaction snapshot and enqueue only heads whose exact evidence IDs use the linked batch. |
| How is `degC_min` computed? | Copy the selected excursion revision's `degree_minutes_low/high` as decimal strings after checking policy, coverage and evidence eligibility. Do not integrate an interpolated chart, derive from duration alone or use private trajectory. Preserve a proved lower bound with unknown upper as in Q4. `NO_EXCURSION_OBSERVED` has no exposure row; no episode means `UNKNOWN` summary if the selection is otherwise incomplete. |
| How does revision identity work? | Hash the sorted exact accepted IDs with their SUPPORT/CONTEXT/EXCLUDED uses and reasons, Finding/episode/assessment UUIDs and basis hashes, selected window/cutoff, `cold-exposure/1`, quantity bounds, aggregate source class/gate digest, and explicit missing cold assumption markers. Existing identical `(finding_revision_id,kind,basis_sha256)` returns its ID. A changed basis appends `revision_no=max+1` and `prior_revision_id` under the work advisory lock. Never overwrite; reversion to a previously used basis must remain audit-visible, so include the newly selected cutoff/revision ID in the hash. |
| What exactly is pending and when does a work item finish? | Unfinished means no `SUCCEEDED` attempt. Include any relevant PENDING/LEASED/FAILED W2-03 cold assessment job and any cold consequence work with no success; a failed attempt does not clear pending. Relevant means same tenant/Site, overlapping half-open selected window and room. Select work in `(enqueued_at,id)` order, lock its UUID, and use `retry_due_at` from the last attempt; no row status UPDATE. An episode-only no-op success has `[]` IDs. |
| Which source/cutoff gates apply? | Resolve S4-05 aggregate provenance from the exact evidence IDs, not Site mode or a Lab manifest. Recompute after a new publication link. Return historical technical rows at an older explicit `known_at` with the historical label; never call their amount current. Closed disclosure gives 403 before returning restricted accepted IDs; mixed/unknown classification and pending/stale currentness withhold a current money claim. No cold price exists even with coherent simulation. |
| What does `RECORDED_REPAIR` mean here? | It is schema reserved only. Neither a W2-03 start Finding nor mock WR-019 is an accepted, costed work record. No `RECORDED_REPAIR` row, repair amount, currency, incident or maintenance item is synthesized in W2-04. |
| How does the API keep one snapshot? | Authenticate and scope Site first. Open one repeatable-read transaction; capture latest committed S2 disposition watermark once, resolve paired window and optional `known_at`, then call W2-03 read/store, Foundation, source provenance and consequence read methods with the same connection. If W2-03 exposes only HTTP calls, add a caller-connection read method to its existing assessment adapter; never invoke loopback HTTP for composition or import a SQL driver into `cold_site_reads.py`. |
| What is a valid explicit selection/cursor? | `from,to,known_at` are strict UTC instants; both window bounds or neither, `from<to`, at most 31 days, no unknown query keys. `known_at` cannot exceed the captured committed watermark for claims; a future cutoff is 422 `COLD_TIME_INVALID`. Cursor stores exact canonical selection/basis and `(source_time,evidence_id)`; a well-formed cursor for another selection or changed basis is 409. Page after the tuple, never by offset. Empty selected evidence is 200 `UNKNOWN`; unavailable/corrupt storage is 503, not empty. |
| What do `as_of` and contact mean? | For an accepted record, `as_of=received_at` (with separate `source_time`); for assessment/episode/Finding, use immutable revision `created_at`; for consequence use its `created_at`; for a configured policy use effective revision time; for a missing value use selected `known_at` and a limitation. Source contact uses only an identified source-specific diagnostic at/before cutoff; otherwise `UNKNOWN`, even if a gateway is online. Accepted fact age is `to - latest qualifying source_time`, separate from contact. |
| Where do exact links go? | Only emit a clickable target after an integration test proves the target route renders that exact ID with Site, window and cutoff preserved. For an unproved cold record or assessment target, display the exact ID as labelled text plus `Analysis view not available for this cold record`; Finding and Site Evidence links that pass their own route proof remain clickable. Never turn a mock Action, Incident, Maintenance or unbuilt Cooling destination into a link. |

Use `cold_site_reads.py` as a pure composition service, and put SQL in the existing assessment/consequence adapters. `financials/cold_recompute.py` receives store protocols and no SQL driver. The five GETs are composed in `main.py`; do not change the mini-grid routers. Run architecture/dependency, workflow, writer guard and targeted import probes after each owning commit. The review packet states the exact migration SHA, W2-03 predecessor revision, replay manifest IDs, accepted IDs, selected revision IDs and test database name.

## Screen-outward planning gate

The [v6.9 screen realization map](../frontend/docs/architecture/v69-screen-realization-map.md), [screen ledger](../frontend/docs/architecture/v69-screen-ledger.json), [model homes](../frontend/docs/architecture/v69-model-homes.json) and [panel contracts](../frontend/docs/architecture/v69-panel-contracts.json) are Architect planning overlays, not accepted screen completion. The owner approved `Real with honest gaps` as the W1 target for 27 screens, including six moved from W4, and their exact core keys/values; later-wave tiers remain pending. The manifest ID and its `visual_reference` key each later comparison; `GAP` in a panel contract means no supported claim yet. Run `python frontend/docs/architecture/check_v69_ledger.py` after ledger changes.

For each `Deferred` screen, the ledger's `promotion_dependencies.to_candidate` lists the design, projection, fixture and task gates before it can enter the executable queue. For every proposed `Real with honest gaps` screen, `promotion_dependencies.to_real` names unresolved panels and remaining work before full mock fidelity can be claimed. A named S task alone does not satisfy that gate. The Planner checks these fields when refining a packet and updates them when a dependency is met or the owner changes a tier.

S1 and S2 are merged; W1 owner input and `A-S3-dispatch` are recorded. **Before S3-01 is activated**, pass PRE-S3-03/startup guards and check the split [V-01 umbrella](V-01-v69-visual-fidelity.md). S5-01 owns selected-window context/timeline/money; S5-02 integrates the list with separate empty and positive fixtures. S6-01 owns Action detail/activity/change, S6-02 owns plan/evidence/outcome, and S6-03 owns the Site Work list. Resolve only model gaps merited by the next supported claim; broader work, domains and indexes stay in later waves. A target tier does not authorize an empty route or illustrative mock value as product data.

S2-02 refinement compared `queue_baseline_nodes`: `I-accepted-evidence-store`, `I-edge-diagnostics-store` and `I-S2-02` remain in S2-02; S2-01b/c retain their nodes. None leaves the baseline. ## Architect dry-read resolution (2026-10-18; governs any earlier ambiguous wording)

**QA-QD amendment (2026-10-18; governs the W2-05a commit-1 handoff).**

- **QA, timezone:** Use `Etc/UTC` as the EV-LAB-001 Site timezone and as both schedule `time_zone` values, with `utc_offset_minutes=0`. It is an IANA Area/Location name accepted by the shared Site parser. Do not widen that parser for bare `UTC`; replace the earlier fixture wording `UTC` wherever it denotes a Site or schedule zone. UTC timestamps and offset-zero semantics are unchanged.
- **QB, property kinds:** `ev-charger-max-power`, `ev-connector-max-power`, `ev-meter-resolution`, `ev-meter-error-bound` and `ev-clock-error-bound` are `PHYSICAL`. `ev-site-import-limit`, `ev-status-cadence` and `ev-meter-cadence` are `CONTROL`. `ev-connector-enabled` remains `CONTROL`. These are definition kinds, independent of whether a value is currently observed.
- **QC, absent feed:** A Site with no `AC_BUS` may publish a declared charger, meter and connector as an incomplete configuration, provided all declared charger/connector properties and schedule entries are valid. More than one parent for a meter, charger or connector always refuses publication. Once a feed is declared, every declared meter must have exactly that feed as its parent and every declared charger must have exactly one path through a meter from that feed; an unfed meter or charger refuses `EV_CONFIGURATION_INVALID`. Any nonempty connector service schedule requires a complete feedâ†’meterâ†’chargerâ†’connector path, even when the Site has no feed.
- **QD, feed cardinality:** Refuse a second `AC_BUS` in an EV Foundation with `EV_CONFIGURATION_INVALID` and a path to the extra feed. The selected response has one `feed`, and no arbitrary feed selection or merged limit is valid. Zero or one feed is publishable subject to the rules above; Draft still requires the feed and its limit.

Build in reviewable commits: **1 vocabulary, parser, typed schedule and validator; 2 EV roles, closed v4 channel matrix, binding publication/snapshot and fixture; 3 selected API; 4 three UI routes and visual proof; 5 migration and final guards/tests.** Commit 5 may be prepared only after W2-04 `0023` is merged into this branch. No interim EV migration is permitted; `0024_w2_ev_config` is reserved for 05a. Run each commit's focused checks and hand off before the next builder run.

**Q1, connector identity.** `BINDING_CHANNEL_OVERLAP` and `EV_CONNECTOR_MISMATCH` stay unchanged. In EV-LAB-001 the c1 tuples are `(c1-charger-controller,session-event)`, `(c1-connector-controller,fault-event|state|requested-power|allocated-limit)`, `(c1-connector-meter,energy|power)`; c2 uses the identical signal names with `c2-` device prefixes. Each of these three devices and seven channels per connector has `component_id=c1` or `c2` respectively and binds to that same EV_CONNECTOR asset. `(site-meter,import)` has `component_id=site-meter-1`, binds to its METER asset, and is the sole Site import channel. `charger-1` is topology and ratings only; it owns no connector channel. Each tuple is a distinct exact entry in `V4_CHANNEL_MAPPINGS`; no prefix wildcard or runtime-generated accepted tuple. Keep the two old unsuffixed W2-00 reserved tuples for their existing tests, label their roles, but do not bind them in this fixture. The v4 snapshot metadata must come from the exact entry. S2's existing one-binding connector check continues to compare the envelope connector asset ID to c1 or c2.

**Q2, readiness.** `CONFIGURATION_INCOMPLETE` applies to `CONNECTOR_NOT_DECLARED`, `FEED_OR_LIMIT_MISSING`, `METER_NOT_BOUND`, `SESSION_EVENTS_NOT_BOUND`, or `STATUS_NOT_BOUND`; `SITE_IMPORT_NOT_BOUND` is a nonblocking capability message under `READY_TO_REPORT`, as are `SOURCE_NOT_CONTACTED` and `COMMISSIONING_UNCONFIRMED`. Missing optional fault, connector power, requested power or allocated limit yields no readiness code; the exact capability that needs it stays unavailable. Required energy, event and state bindings are per declared connector. A configured Site may be ready while source contact and commissioning remain unknown.

**Q3, absent properties.** Missing `ev-site-import-limit` on an otherwise valid feed is the sole publishable numeric gap and emits `FEED_OR_LIMIT_MISSING`; absence of feed or all connectors is likewise publishable as configuration-incomplete so the selected read can explain it. For every *declared* charger/connector, missing `ev-charger-max-power`, `ev-connector-max-power`, `ev-connector-enabled`, `ev-meter-resolution`, `ev-meter-error-bound`, `ev-status-cadence`, `ev-meter-cadence` or `ev-clock-error-bound` refuses Foundation publication with `EV_CONFIGURATION_INVALID` and a path to that property. Present wrong type/unit, nonfinite/out-of-range value, invalid topology or schedule uses the same typed refusal. Do not pretend a missing physical or clock parameter is a readiness finding. A Site with no declared connector cannot publish a binding set or Draft a Lab run.

**Q4, cadence.** `ev-status-cadence` on each connector converts min to seconds and must be `0 < value <= 1`; it is the published state-channel cadence. `ev-meter-cadence` converts min to seconds and must be `0 < value <= 5`; it governs connector energy, connector power, Site import, requested power and allocated limit, all of which publish aligned 300-second *maximum* slots for this profile; the fixture declares exactly 5 min. Event channels have null cadence. `BindingRequest` has no cadence field: derive `bindings[].cadence_seconds` only from the selected Foundation property. Reject a property above its ceiling at Foundation publication (`EV_CONFIGURATION_INVALID`); reject any future submitted cadence field as `BINDING_REQUEST_INVALID`, not an invented `BINDING_CADENCE_INVALID`. `ev-clock-error-bound` is positive seconds and is recorded as the selected configured tolerance; 05a makes no observed clock-attestation claim. No cadence is inferred from observed timestamps.

**Q5, schedule.** Add `connector_enable_schedules` to `foundation_parsing.py:FOUNDATION_CONTENT_KEYS` and both parser allowlists through that shared constant; it is not `site_controls`. Exactly one schedule entry per declared connector, including a disabled connector (which has an empty `weekly` array); an enabled connector may have an empty weekly array, meaning no service hours. Each entry's zone equals the Site's IANA `timezone`. The fixture zone is `Etc/UTC`, weekly TUESDAY 08:00â€“16:00 with offset 0 for both c1/c2, so it recurs on Tuesdays during the revision's effective period, not just 6 October. For a bounded effective interval, enumerate each occurrence and validate offset and real, unambiguous local endpoints throughout that interval. For an open-ended interval, permit only zones whose offset is fixed for all future occurrences (`Etc/UTC` qualifies); a DST zone needs a bounded revision and a successor when its offset changes. Reject overlap, invalid endpoint and missing entry as `EV_CONFIGURATION_INVALID`. At selected `at`, the effective revision supplies its own schedule; never merge schedules across revisions.

**Q6, fixtures.** 05a creates `backend/tests/fixtures/w2/ev-lab-001.yaml` and registers the Site in its focused test/setup path. There is one Site, `EV-LAB-001`: the stocked Foundation and published binding revision are its first complete basis. Missing meter/event/status examples are separate *test-created binding revisions* on that same Site, with nonoverlapping effective periods after the 6 October complete-run window; the missing-limit example is a later Foundation revision on the same Site. Tests use isolated stores/DBs and pin `at` and revision IDs, so 05b's complete 6 October basis is untouched. No new Site codes are introduced. A revision never rewrites the original. 05b adds scenarios and uses this fixture, not a second copy.

**Q7, migration order.** W2-04 owns `0023`; 05a reserves `0024_w2_ev_config` now. Vocabulary/API/UI commits may proceed before 0023, but do not generate or test 0024 against 0022. Merge reviewed 0023 into the 05a branch, create `0024` with `down_revision` pointing to 0023, then run upgrade/downgrade and final tests. 05b adds no migration.

**Q8, kinds and profile.** `ev_connector_energy` has role `value_kind=INTERVAL_DELTA`, source/canonical unit kWh, parameter-free `IDENTITY_KWH` that accepts only kWh. Other EV interval roles use `value_kind=NUMBER`, `IDENTITY`, kW and v4 `INTERVAL_MEAN`; STATE uses `ENUM`, and EVENT uses `IDENTITY`. `(cX-connector-meter,energy)` requires nonnull session and connector in v4; power and controller interval channels require connector and carry session when a session exists; Site import has explicit-null session/connector. Preserve existing `V4_MAPPING_PROFILE_ID=simulator-lab-gateway-cold` for cold and its historical snapshots; EV binds under the new exact `simulator-lab-gateway-ev/1` profile, with an explicit profile-to-closed-table lookup. Do not mutate cold profile/version or v3 bytes. 05b registers the producer for that EV profile.

With a declared feed, every meter and charger needs its full feedâ†’meterâ†’charger path; without a feed, an unfed meter or charger is publishable only as incomplete configuration and no connector may have scheduled service hours. Define properties and carriers exactly: `ev-site-import-limit` kW on `AC_BUS` (CONTROL); `ev-charger-max-power` kW on `EV_CHARGER` (PHYSICAL); `ev-connector-max-power` kW (PHYSICAL) and `ev-connector-enabled` state (CONTROL) on `EV_CONNECTOR`; `ev-meter-resolution` and `ev-meter-error-bound` kWh on `EV_CONNECTOR` (PHYSICAL); `ev-status-cadence` and `ev-meter-cadence` min on `EV_CONNECTOR` (CONTROL), plus `ev-clock-error-bound` s on `EV_CONNECTOR` (PHYSICAL). Current `models.py:ComponentProperty.value` is numeric: extend that typed value to number-or-state and make `foundation_parsing.py:parse_component_properties,render_component_properties` branch only for `ev-connector-enabled`. Its value is the exact string `ENABLED|DISABLED`, unit `state`, kind CONTROL; all preexisting numeric properties keep identical parser/rendered bytes. The first three limits, meter resolution/cadences and clock bound are strictly positive finite values; meter error bound nonnegative finite. The selected fixture has feed limit 80 kW, two connector/charger ratings 60 kW, resolution/error bound 0.001 kWh, status cadence 1 min, meter cadence 5 min and clock error bound 30 s. A real Site must author these values; the pack has no silent production default. Schema change `0024_w2_ev_config` follows `0023`, adds the partial `(site_id,session_id,connector_id,source_time,id)` EV measurement index, retains existing Foundation history and 0020 family CHECK. Downgrade refuses with EV measurements, then drops the index while retaining historical Foundation reader safety. No new configuration SQL table.

Represent the connector enable schedule as a typed, time-valid Foundation control named `connector_enable_schedules`, an array of `{connector_asset_id,time_zone,weekly:[{weekday,local_start,local_end,utc_offset_minutes}]}`. `weekday` is uppercase MONDAYâ€¦SUNDAY, local times are `HH:MM`, intervals are half-open within one local day, `time_zone` is the Site IANA zone, and the explicit offset must match that zone for every occurrence in the Foundation revision's effective date range; publish a new revision when the offset changes. The fixture declares both connectors enabled TUESDAY 08:00â€“16:00, UTC offset 0, for 2026-10-06. Reject overlap, reversed/zero interval, ambiguous/nonexistent local instant, disabled connector marked available, and enablement without feed/meter/charger. Selected `at` uses the effective Foundation and binding revision at that instant; a missing selector uses the existing current-selection rule. Older revisions remain selectable and never inherit new limits/schedule. A configured service window is not observed availability.

## 3. W2-05b versioned charger/session producer

Add `ev-charger/1` `ModelSpec`, `ev-publication/1`, `ev-observation/1` to the part-1 closed host registry, preserving all existing model identities (`host/execution_adapter.py:123-149`; `.agent/W2-technical-design-cold.md:59-69`). Reject unknown pack/profile/parameter version before Draft. Frozen run identity includes Foundation/binding/source IDs, scenario SHA, pack/profile/observation versions, UTC window and seed. Stage seals only public v4 reports; registered Commit â†’ SQLite outbox â†’ authenticated Batch V2 â†’ S2 accepted evidence. No direct evidence/Finding seed, Lab private state, vehicle/customer identity or hidden demand in envelopes (`host/lab_execution.py:2154-2164,2428-2501`; `frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md:131,183`).

**Discrete model.** One-minute UTC step, exact decimal arithmetic; default fixture has two 60 kW connectors, 80 kW site import cap, both enabled [08:00,16:00) UTC on 2026-10-06, site non-EV base load 0 kW. State per connector: `UNPLUGGED|PLUGGED|AUTHORIZING|CHARGING|FAULTED`, session ID or null, authorization result, requested kW, allocated kW, meter accumulator kWh, fault latch. Private forcing: plug/unplug, authorization accept/deny, request schedule, fault/clear, grid interruption, publication dropout/latency. Initial unplugged, no session/fault, accumulator 0. At each minute: apply forcing ordered `(time,connector,kind)`; a plug assigns next deterministic scoped session ID; authorization takes 1 minute; acceptance emits START when CHARGING begins; denial produces no START and is a contextual observed state, not a failed session. Allocate shared available power `max(0,site_limit-base_load)` by connector ID ascending in round-robin 1 kW quanta among charging connectors up to `min(request,connector_limit,charger_limit)`; persist round-robin pointer so no connector monopolizes successive minutes. `E_next=E+allocated_kW/60`, exact kWh. A fault latches FAULTED, emits FAULT and ABORT for an active started session; explicit user unplug emits END (completed) only after active charge and no fault; grid interruption pauses allocation and connector state, it does not invent ABORT. Fault clear requires explicit forcing and emits CLEAR; a new plug creates a new session. Simultaneous END/ABORT or START twice for one ID is prohibited by simulator sanity guard. Fail run on negative energy, allocated sum above available/site/connector limits, energy residual, state with no valid session, duplicate conflicting forcing or non-monotone time.

**Public transform.** `ev-publication/1`: connector state at transitions and every minute; connector interval energy delta over aligned five-minute `[start,end)` slots (including zero while an active accepted session pauses), with session ID in the W2-00 v4 measurement payload; power mean per slot and site import mean per slot; session/fault events at observed transitions. Every v4 measurement contains `session_id,connector_id`; both are nonnull for connector energy and explicit null on cold/site channels. Connector ID must equal the bound EV_CONNECTOR asset; S2 refuses `EV_CONNECTOR_MISMATCH`. `source_time=interval_end` for interval reports. Split a session boundary inside a slot into nonoverlapping subintervals. Round accumulator to 0.001 kWh half-even at both ends and difference rounded values, preserving additive deltas; meter bound 0.001 kWh per boundary. Event IDs derive from scenario SHA, channel and transition ordinal; retransmission preserves IDs/bytes. Observation gap drops a channel report, never changes the world; delayed report retains source time and message identity. Mapping `simulator-lab-gateway-ev/1` exactly allows `(charger-controller,session-event)`, `(connector-controller,fault-event)`, `(connector-controller,state)`, `(connector-meter,energy)`, `(connector-meter,power)`, `(site-meter,import)`, `(connector-controller,requested-power)`, `(connector-controller,allocated-limit)` with listed kinds/units/cadences (`simulator/assetops_simulator/gateway/mappings.py:22-46,87-107`).

| --- | --- | --- |

All scenarios use `ev-scenario/1`, frozen window/seed/profile and initial unplugged/no-session/no-fault/0 kWh state. Enabled schedule is [08:00,16:00) UTC; c1/c2 each max 60 kW and Site cap 80 kW, base load 0. The single charging connector receives 60 kW every active minute. `simulator/assetops_simulator/observation/transform.py` owns `ev-observation/1` hold/drop/fault variants; they alter public reports only. No mock 12/10/1/1, 120 kWh or $36 is injected (`frontend/mockups/v69/screens.js:433-450`). `Role.value_kind` includes `EVENT` and `INTERVAL_DELTA`; EVENT conversion is `IDENTITY` with outcome allowlist, delta conversion is `IDENTITY_KWH` with exact decimal and no counter interpretation. Lab persisted-state validator uses the EV connector state vocabulary of `ev-charger/1`, not the mini-grid generator lifecycle.

## 4. W2-06 session correlation, meter sum, Finding, currentness

Select only accepted, GOOD, clock-attested records with valid effective Foundation/binding and exact `(tenant,site,charger,connector,session_id)`; EVENT session ID comes from W2-00, energy identity from the v4 measurement extension above. Require one START, at most one terminal END or ABORT, ordered by source time with <=30-second declared cross-source clock error; a terminal without START remains orphan context, not a session. An END is COMPLETED only when same scoped ID, no competing ABORT, and no contradictory state; explicit ABORT proves OBSERVED_ABORT, while contemporaneous fault on the same connector/session is additionally required for a **fault-associated** Finding. Fault alone does not prove an abort. Missing terminal is INCOMPLETE regardless of apparently idle status; conflicting good terminal/start times or incompatible connector identity is CONTRADICTORY. `SUSPECT` and unbound reports are context/excluded with reasons, never settle outcomes. Repeat events are deduped by W2-00 and cross-tenant/session collisions cannot join.

For each session, intersect GOOD connector `INTERVAL_DELTA` reports with `[start,terminal)` and same session ID; accept only wholly contained, nonoverlapping half-open intervals with finite `0<=kWh<=connector_max_kW*duration_hours+2*meter_error_bound`, and matching exact source. Do **not** pro-rate a report spanning a boundary, choose between conflicting duplicates, substitute power integration or infer zero for an absent slot. `supported_kwh=sum(exact accepted deltas)`; `unknown_meter_seconds` is the union duration of uncovered active 5-minute slots, clipped to session bounds. A delivered-energy total is **complete** only if every active slot is covered (partial boundary slots must have a split report) and no contradiction; otherwise report known partial sum with `energy_complete=false` and unknown time, never call it total delivered. If no supported intervals, quantity null rather than zero. Session outcome counts use START denominator, separately completed/observed abort/incomplete/contradictory; orphan records are separate. No availability percentage or site constraint cause in W2. Synchronized site import below limit is context only; a power-constraint claim requires independent accepted requested and allocated-limit signals plus site import over the same slots, and W2 still labels competing causes unknown (`.agent/architect-W2-design.md:37-49`).

`ev-session/1` assessment basis SHA sorts accepted evidence IDs+content digests, excluded/context IDs+reasons, effective Foundation/binding/mapping IDs, model/rule versions, `[from,to)`, `known_at` and source classification. Session revision and its evidence/interval links append atomically with `assessment_revision` and any FindingRevision. A fault-abort Finding uses the stable key above, with exact fault/abort/START evidence and limitation â€œfault observed; component cause and unmet demand unknown.â€ A completed late END supersedes prior INCOMPLETE by new revision; a contradictory terminal withdraws previous current conclusion. Worker enqueue on **every** newly accepted relevant EV report, including late source time; until latest applicable job settles, previous projection reads `PENDING_RECOMPUTE`, with historical exact revision separately selectable. For current status, latest needed connector state <=2 minutes old at read time and terminal/event sources within declared cadence; old closed sessions may remain historical conclusions. Current service-window coverage uses one-minute status slots and explicit `known_seconds/unknown_seconds`; no available-time inference over gaps >2 minutes. Source gate follows S4-05 exact revision provenance; generated and authored evidence are labelled and mixed/unknown blocks a current positive (`.ai/DECISIONS.md:5-15,4165-4188`).

## 5. W2-07 tariff scenario and claim gate

`ev_gross_tariff_per_kwh` is a Site time-valid, recorded revision in `currency/kWh`, with authored basis/source; no default and no billing/collection identity. A window may price only supported energy in completed or observed-abort sessions, each with complete meter coverage and settled current assessment; no session interval is counted twice. For every included meter interval, select exactly one tariff revision whose **valid** range covers it and whose **recorded** range is visible at `known_at`; W2 v1 requires the same revision and currency across the entire priced window, otherwise `UNPRICED/PRICE_GAP_OR_CHANGE` (no averaging). Formula `amount = Î£ exact interval kWh Ã— tariff value`, unrounded in storage; display rounding only. `quantity_kwh` and exact session revision/accepted meter evidence/tariff revision IDs are pinned. No lost-sales estimate: private requested power, incomplete sessions and fault downtime do not measure counterfactual demand. An aborted session can contribute **delivered** pre-abort energy, never lost energy. W1 LR current-money gate and S4-05 coherent source gate apply: pending/late/revised assessment, conflicting meter, historical cutoff, mixed/unknown provenance, unsupported tariff, or missing price â†’ `WITHHELD` or `UNPRICED`, null amount (not zero). Historical amount may appear labelled historical only under its exact old basis, never as today's current money. `overlap_group='ev:'+sha256(canonical(tenant_id,site_id,window_start,window_end,tariff_revision_id))` prevents adding the same meter intervals through multiple Findings; Site scenario is one window revision, not per-Finding additive totals (`backend/migrations/versions/0010_financial_assumptions.py:38-102`; `.ai/DECISIONS.md:5-15`).

## 6. Selected reads and refusals

All routes are tenant-authenticated Site-code reads. Except Foundation/replay, require UTC half-open `from,to`, max 31 days, optional UTC `known_at` (default latest committed watermark); a historical cutoff is labelled historical. Common response `{site_id,window:{from,to,known_at},currentness:{state,watermark,latest_relevant_evidence_at,pending_since},source_provenance,limitations,...}`. Watermark pins latest included S2 decision time + assessment revision; lists use opaque `(time,id)` cursor, default limit 50/max 200, `{items,next_cursor}`. Shared error `{error:{code,message}}`: 401 unauthenticated, 403 wrong tenant/Lab gate/source-gated detail, 404 missing/wrong Site type or record, 409 unresolved selected revision or conflicting current recompute, 422 bad parameter/window/selector, 503 ledger/projection unavailable. Valid evidence gaps return 200 with UNKNOWN/null and reasons. No endpoint returns private forcing/oracle, customer/vehicle or a fabricated zero (`.agent/W2-technical-design-cold.md:83-107`; `backend/assetops_backend/evidence_api.py:54-59,157-161`).
